findings.title: The L07-A03 fix leaves #903's own Agent Brief AC2 unmet: watermark is now a documented half-state, which the brief explicitly forbids
findings.evidence: #903's newest Agent Brief (gh issue view 903, 2026-09-17T17:00:15Z comment) states AC2 verbatim: 'watermark is either fully wired to a renderer or fully absent from the types; a grep proves no dangling reference' and Desired behavior: '...unless the implementer finds a real consumer, in which case it is threaded through the hook to that consumer; no half-state where it is typed but dropped.' The original build (6f62346e) satisfied this literally by deleting the field (fully absent). The fix round's L07-A03 response restores watermark?: unknown on ReviewQueueEnvelope (apps/web/lib/firm/needs-you.ts:245-254) but confirms via its own new test cell (use-review-queue.test.ts:98-104, assert.doesNotMatch(hookSource, /\.watermark\b/)) that use-review-queue.ts still never reads it - i.e. no consumer was found or wired. That is precisely the state the brief calls a forbidden half-state ('typed but dropped'), just now a NAMED one instead of a silent one. L07-A03's own required_fix offered two forks ('restore the field and render it' OR 'keep the deletion and document the honesty gap'); the fix round took neither literally - it restored without rendering. This does mirror the pre-existing compliance?: unknown / lint?: unknown siblings in the same type (a real, older house pattern for this exact envelope), which is a reasonable engineering tradeoff, but it is not what ticket #903's own binding brief asks for, and neither fixround-1.md nor the type's own comment says so.
findings.required_fix: Either thread watermark through use-review-queue.ts to a real consumer (satisfying 'fully wired to a renderer'), or revert to full deletion and instead record the CONTEXT.md/estate-concept honesty gap as prose in apps/web/README.md or a code comment near the deletion site (satisfying 'fully absent from the types' while fixing L07-A03's complaint about the false justification) - not both partially. If the compliance/lint precedent is judged to make the half-state acceptable going forward, that judgement should be stated against #903's AC2 explicitly, not left implicit.

findings.title: fixround-1.md's description of the confirmed-pre-existing axe flake undercounts it: it is 4 nodes across two UI regions with two different ratios, not one node at one ratio
findings.evidence: Independently re-ran document-correction-walk twice (full file and standalone with -g). The full-file run reproduces the exact 14 passed / 1 failed count fixround-1.md reports, and the failure is confirmed order-dependent (passes standalone), matching the report's overall verdict of 'confirmed pre-existing flake, not a regression.' However the actual axe violation object carries 4 nodes: two on the selected revision-table row (bgColor #f5f6f4, fgColor #6c7575, ratio 4.36, on the 'done' status chip and the 'filed by a human' date cell) and two on the Facts card's field-name labels (bgColor #ffffff, fgColor #727a7a, ratio 4.39, on 'invoice.total' and 'invoice.vendor_name'). fixround-1.md's L07-A01 section describes it as singular: 'a color-contrast axe violation (text-muted-foreground on bg-muted, 4.49 vs the 4.5 AA threshold, on a selected revision-table row in the Facts tab).' Neither the exact ratio (4.49) nor the bg-muted background nor the single-node count matches what a fresh run actually produces. This does not change the verdict (still pre-existing, still order-dependent, still outside this lane's diff - neither the Facts-card labels file nor the revision-table file appears in git diff dd3f8f1d..HEAD), but the follow-up ticket the report recommends filing should be filed against the real shape (2 locations, 2 ratios), not the narrower one described.
findings.required_fix: When filing the recommended follow-up ticket for this contrast debt, correct the reproduction data (4 nodes, 2 locations, ratios 4.36 and 4.39) rather than copying fixround-1.md's description verbatim.

summary: Recheck confirms every one of the 15 review findings (8 spec-lens, 7 adversarial-lens, excluding notes) that fixround-1.md claims fixed is fixed, verified independently by source inspection plus re-running: pnpm typecheck (clean), pnpm lint (exit 0), the full apps/web unit suite (4664/4666 pass, 2 pre-existing skips - exact match), and all three named e2e walks on the lane's own Playwright triple (12/22/14+1 passed - exact match, including independently re-confirming the one document-correction-walk axe failure is the same order-dependent, pre-existing flake via a standalone -g run). Nothing the fix round touched broke anything else. Two minor items remain open, neither blocking: (1) #903's own Agent Brief AC2 ('fully wired to a renderer or fully absent from the types; no half-state') is not literally satisfied by the L07-A03 fix, which restored watermark as a typed-but-unread field - a documented half-state that mirrors the file's own compliance/lint precedent but is not one of the two forks that finding's own required_fix offered, and the brief's own wording forbids it; (2) fixround-1.md's description of the disclosed pre-existing axe flake (single node, 4.49, bg-muted) undercounts what a fresh run actually shows (4 nodes across two UI regions, ratios 4.36 and 4.39) - the verdict (pre-existing, order-dependent, out of this lane's diff) still holds, but the reproduction data quoted for a future follow-up ticket is not accurate. Verdict: accept (nothing above minor remains).
